sources.note: Aguna/Agouna is not among the 49 Gbe varieties analysed; 'stress' occurs only as Kruskal's MDS stress. Appendix (printed p. 110 = PDF p. 117): word-list items entered without tone though tone was transcribed. Note: hh.bib tags Kluge 2006 with 'Awlan = Aguna [aug]'; this is a mislabel -- Awlan in Kluge is the Anlo Ewe variety of Ghana (printed p. 8: 'Standard Ewe is based on Awlan, the most prestigious variety of the Ewe cluster').

sources.citation: Faton, Gabriele R. 2012. Aguna Speakers in Benin: A Sociolinguistic Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-042. Dallas: SIL International. 25 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey only (2002 fieldwork, written 2006). Sec. 1.1 p. 1: 'To the best of our knowledge, no publications about or in the Aguna language existed at the time of the survey.' Sec. 1.2 pp. 1-2: Capo 1986 marks Aguna 'not Gbe'; Capo 1990:1 lists it among the Gbe languages of Benin; no research on Agou-Aguna relationship; alt. names Awuna, Agunaco, Agunan-o, Agunagbe. No tone or stress remarks anywhere.

sources.note: Nothing. Classification tables only (Capo 1986:101 five clusters, Table 1 p. 4; Stewart 1994; Kluge 2005-2007, Tables 3-4). Aguna appears in no table, i.e. it is outside both Capo's 19-variety sample and Kluge's 49-variety sample.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 2000. The New Ewe Orthography: based on the Gbe Uniform Standard Orthography. Cape Town: CASAS.
